question.text: The 'fit and proper person' criteria for trading membership is laid down in:

explanation.text: The Logic: Trading-member admission requires fulfilment of the fit and proper person criteria laid down in the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008. Schedule II of those regulations sets out the specific fit-and-proper considerations. The Trap: The Companies Act, FEMA and the RBI Act govern different domains (corporate formation, foreign exchange and central banking). The fit-and-proper test for intermediaries sits squarely under SEBI regulations. Note: Keep general admission criteria distinct from fit-and-proper criteria. General admission looks at age, capital adequacy, education and experience; the Schedule II fit-and-proper considerations cover integrity, reputation and character, absence of convictions or restraint orders, competence including financial solvency and net worth, and absence of wilful-defaulter categorisation.
